It is Medinan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1} {The King, the Holy One, the Mighty, the Wise}. That is: all that is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah, submits to His command, takes Him as God, and worships Him, because He is the Perfect King, to whom belongs the dominion of the higher and lower worlds; all of them are His possessions and under His management. Al-Quddus (the Holy One): the One who is exalted and free from every defect and imperfection. Al-Aziz (the Mighty): the One who overpowers all things. Al-Hakim (the Wise): in His creation and His command. These great attributes call to the worship of Allah alone, with no partner.

{2} ﴿He it is who has sent among the unlettered (al-ummiyyin) a messenger﴾. The meaning of "al-ummiyyin" is those who have no scripture and no trace of a message, among the Arabs and others who are not People of the Book. Allah bestowed upon them a great favour, greater than His favour upon others, because they lacked knowledge and goodness. They were in ﴿clear error﴾: they worshipped idols, trees and stones, and they had the character of ravenous beasts, where the strong devoured the weak. They were in utter ignorance of the sciences of the prophets. So Allah sent among them a messenger from among them, whose lineage, beautiful attributes and truthfulness they knew, and He sent down His Book to him. ﴿He recites to them His verses﴾, which are decisive and necessitate faith and certainty; ﴿and purifies them﴾, by setting out for them the noble morals, urging them towards them, and restraining them from base morals; ﴿and teaches them the Book and the wisdom﴾, that is, the knowledge of the Book and the Sunnah (the Prophetic example and teachings), which comprises the sciences of the earlier and later generations. After this teaching and purification they became among the most knowledgeable of creation, indeed they became the leaders of the people of knowledge and religion, the most complete in character and the best in guidance and conduct. They were guided themselves and guided others, so they became the leaders of the guided and the guides of the God-fearing. Therefore Allah's favour upon them through the sending of this Messenger is the most perfect blessing and the most exalted gift.

{3} His saying: ﴿and others among them who have not yet joined them﴾ means: He also bestowed His favour upon others, from other than the unlettered, namely those from among the People of the Book and those who would come after them, ﴿who have not yet joined them﴾. This can mean that they have not yet joined them in excellence, and it can mean that they have not yet joined them in time, as far as those who took part in the call of the Messenger. Both meanings are correct, for those among whom Allah sent His Messenger, who witnessed him and took part in his call, obtained such distinctions and virtues that no one can ever attain to.

{4} This is part of His might and wisdom, that He did not leave His servants neglected or aimless, but sent messengers among them, commanding and forbidding them. This is from ﴿the great bounty of Allah﴾, which He gives to whomever He wills among His servants. It is superior to His favour upon them in bodily health, abundance of provision and other worldly blessings. There is no blessing greater than the blessing of religion, which is the source of success and everlasting happiness.

{5} When God mentioned His favour upon this community, to whom He sent the unlettered Prophet, and the distinctions and virtues God specially granted them, in which no one can equal them, namely the unlettered community who surpassed the earlier and later peoples, even the People of the Book who claim to be the learned masters (al-ʿulamaʾ al-rabbaniyyun) and the foremost rabbis (al-ahbar al-mutaqaddimun), He mentioned that those to whom God entrusted the Torah, from among the Jews, and likewise the Christians, and commanded them to learn it and act upon it, but they did not bear it and did not fulfil what they were entrusted with, have no virtue: their likeness is that of the donkey that carries books of knowledge on its back. Does that donkey benefit from those books on its back? Does any virtue accrue to it because of them? Its only share of them is carrying them. This is the likeness of the scholars of the People of the Book who did not act upon what is in the Torah, the most important and greatest part of which is the command to follow Muhammad (ﷺ), to give glad tidings of him, and to believe in what he brought of the Qur'an. Has anyone whose description is this benefited from the Torah except with loss, ruin and the establishment of proof against him? This likeness therefore corresponds to their condition. ﴿Evil is the likeness of the people who denied﴾ Our signs, which indicate the truthfulness of Our Messenger and the soundness of what he brought, ﴿and God does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾; i.e., He does not guide them to their welfare so long as wrongdoing is their attribute and obstinacy their quality.

{6} Among the wrongdoing and obstinacy of the Jews is that they know they are upon falsehood, yet they claim they are upon truth, and that they are the friends of God to the exclusion of the people! Therefore God commanded His Messenger to say to them: If you are truthful in your claim that you are upon the truth and are God's friends, ﴿then wish for death﴾. This is a light command, for if they knew they were upon truth, they would not have hesitated from this challenge, which God made a proof of their truthfulness if they wished for it, and of their lying if they did not.

{7} Since they did not do this despite the announcement made to them, it is known that they are aware of the falsehood and corruption of what they are upon. Therefore He said: ﴿But they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forward﴾; i.e., because of the sins and disobediences for which they shrink from death. ﴿And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾: nothing of their wrongdoing can be hidden from Him.

{8} Moreover, even if they do not wish for death because of what their hands have sent forward, but flee from it in the utmost flight, that will not save them; death will surely meet them, the death which God has decreed upon His servants [and prescribed for them]. Then, after death and the completion of their terms, all creatures will be returned on the Day of Resurrection to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform them of what they used to do, of good and evil, little and much.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 62, verse 9–11:

{9} Allah, exalted is He, commands His believing servants to attend the Friday prayer (Salat al-Jumu'ah), to hasten to it from the time the call to it is made, and to strive toward it. The meaning of "sa'y" (striving) here is hastening to it, giving it attention, and making it the most important of their affairs, not the walking that is forbidden when proceeding to the prayer. His words, ﴿And leave off trade﴾, mean: abandon trading when the call to prayer is made, and proceed to it. ﴿That is better for you﴾ than your occupation with trade or your missing the obligatory prayer, which is among the most emphatic of obligations, ﴿if you knew﴾ that what is with Allah is better and more lasting, and that whoever prefers this world over the religion has truly lost, while thinking that he is gaining.

{10} This command to leave off trade is temporary, for the duration of the prayer. ﴿And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land﴾ to seek provision and commerce. Since occupation with trade is a likely cause of heedlessness of the remembrance of Allah, Allah commanded that His remembrance be increased so that this would compensate for it, saying: ﴿And remember Allah often﴾, meaning in your standing, your sitting, and on your sides, ﴿that you may succeed﴾, for increasing the remembrance of Allah is among the greatest causes of success.

{11} ﴿And when they sight a transaction or amusement, they rush to it﴾, meaning they went out of the mosque eager for that amusement and that trade, and left good behind, ﴿and leave you standing﴾ delivering the khutbah to the people, and that was on Friday. While the Prophet (ﷺ) was delivering the khutbah to the people, a caravan carrying merchandise arrived in Madinah. When the people heard of it while they were in the mosque, they dispersed from the mosque and left the Prophet (ﷺ) delivering the khutbah, hastening toward something that should not have been hastened toward, and it was a breach of etiquette. ﴿Say: What is with Allah﴾ of reward and recompense for whoever adheres to good and restrains himself in the worship of Allah ﴿is better than amusement and than trade﴾, which, even if some of its aims are attained, is only a small and fleeting gain that forfeits the good of the Hereafter. Patience in obedience to Allah does not forfeit provision, ﴿and Allah is the best of providers﴾; so whoever fears Allah, He will provide for him from where he does not expect.

In these verses are many benefits:
Among them: the Friday prayer is an obligation upon [all] believers, and it is obligatory for them to strive toward it, hasten to it, and give attention to its matter.
Among them: the two khutbahs on Friday are an obligation whose attendance is required, because He explained the "dhikr" here as the two khutbahs, and Allah commanded going to it and striving for it.
Among them: the legislation of the call to the Friday prayer and the command to it.
Among them: the prohibition of buying and selling after the Friday call, and the prohibition of that. This is only because it forfeits the obligation and distracts from it. This shows that every matter, even if permissible in origin, if it leads to forfeiting an obligation, is not permissible in that situation.
Among them: the command to attend the two khutbahs on Friday, and the blame of whoever does not attend them; and an inseparable part of this is listening attentively to them.
Among them: it is fitting for the servant who turns to the worship of Allah at a time when the soul calls toward amusements, trades, and desires, to remind it of what is with Allah of good things, and of what is for one who prefers His pleasure over his own desire.

The Tafsir of Surah al-Jumu'ah is complete, by the grace and help of Allah.
And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
